column6: Sigiriya is one of Sri Lanka's most iconic archaeological sites, featuring a massive rock fortress that rises approximately 200 meters above the surrounding plains. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is renowned for its ancient frescoes, landscaped gardens, and remarkable engineering.
column7: Sigiriya was developed during the reign of King Kashyapa I (477–495 CE), who transformed the enormous rock into a royal palace and fortified capital after seizing the throne from his father, King Dhatusena. The complex included sophisticated water gardens, terraced gardens, defensive moats, and elaborate palace structures atop the rock. After King Kashyapa's death in 495 CE, Sigiriya reverted to a Buddhist monastery and remained an important religious site until about the 14th century. Today, it is considered one of the finest examples of ancient urban planning and engineering in South Asia.
